use_case: Pipeline leak-detection anomaly module: scores 1-minute pressure, flow, and valve data for each of 4 pipeline segments and alerts controllers to a possible leak
vendor_or_model: Hosted SCADA vendor's anomaly detection module (machine learning, not generative), tuned by the vendor on 12 months of company historian data; runs in the vendor's hosted SCADA platform
data_categories: SCADA historian data (pressures, flows, valve states); no personal information
affects_individuals: No (indirectly: people living and working along the pipeline)
human_in_the_loop: Advisory only. The controller treats each alert as a prompt to check SCADA trends and, if needed, send field staff; the model cannot command field devices or change alarms
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 192.615(a)(12) (rupture identification procedures must name information sources); 49 CFR 192.631(d) (fatigue from night alerts; reduced-scope procedures); 49 CFR 192.605(c) (abnormal operation); 192.705 and 192.706 remain the required patrol and leakage survey methods; FTC Act Section 5 (vendor accuracy claims, indirect)

use_case: Public generative AI chatbots used by office staff to draft letters and summaries
data_categories: Risk of Restricted or Internal information (SCADA details, maps, contracts, employee data) being pasted
human_in_the_loop: None needed while no company information is entered
applicable_laws: No AI-specific law; POL-02 C.2 and POL-04 4.7 ban Restricted and Internal information; Fla. Stat. 501.171 if employee personal information were exposed

use_case: Built-in AI writing and summary assistant in the productivity suite (vendor feature, available on the company's plan)
vendor_or_model: Productivity suite vendor's generative AI assistant
data_categories: Email and shared-drive content, which includes Internal and Restricted information
human_in_the_loop: Staff review any drafted text before sending
